video_title: The Economy Is Sending a Surprising Signal? with Mikkel Rosenvold | Macro Mondays
gist: Despite the title promising an economy signal with a guest, this is a solo Macro Mondays monologue covering the midterm losses (37 House seats), a record one-day AI-driven degrossing the speaker thinks may mark a bottom, nowcast data showing inflation rolling over, and skeptical views on Ukraine peace talks and diesel.

insights.claim: The Republicans lost 37 House seats in the midterms, which is large but in line with historical losses for an unpopular president; a president near even approval typically loses 20-26 seats.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: The loss is a normal-cycle outcome, not a regime break, so it does not change the macro narrative.

insights.claim: The speaker argues the midterms do not change the macro outlook because Trump has passed only three major laws in two years (Genius Act, Big Beautiful Bill Act, Secure America Act) and is not focused on lawmaking, so a Democratic House matters less than assumed.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Little legislative change is lost, so portfolio narratives need not be rebuilt around the midterms.

insights.claim: Expect the lame-duck session to be as productive as the past two years, with priority on the 2027 budget and a possible debt ceiling increase; the debt ceiling is expected to bind around late 2027 or early 2028.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Raising the debt ceiling would free Trump's political capital; failure raises shutdown and fiscal-fight risk.

insights.claim: For the rest of Trump's term expect lawfare, impeachment attempts and continued battles over the debt ceiling and spending, and a government shutdown in 2028 is a risk after the last one was very bad for markets.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Position for event-risk volatility around budget deadlines.
insights.quote: Last time we have a government shutdown, it was very, very bad for markets.

insights.claim: Congress is very unlikely to pass anything on tariffs, and big increases in the defense budget are doubtful, which the speaker flags as poor for drone-related holdings.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Tariff relief via legislation is off the table, and defense-spending upside is capped.

insights.claim: Contrarian view that the US will not become a single-party state even if Democrats flip Texas, because single-member districts structurally produce two parties that converge on winning about 51 percent.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Avoid extrapolating one election into permanent political regime change.
insights.quote: the US electoral system simply is built for a two-party system

insights.claim: Republicans lost nearly every demographic, notably young white men under 30 who voted Trump in 2024 but did not turn out; Republicans need roughly 57-58 percent of white voters to win, and a 4-5 percent swing is still achievable in 2028.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: The 2028 map remains competitive; 'death of MAGA' narratives are premature.

insights.claim: The speaker expects Pete Hexath to resign or be sacked, as a scapegoat for the Iran war and to pre-empt a Democratic Congress making loyalist confirmations harder.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Cabinet turnover is a political-risk signal around the Iran conflict.

themes.theme: AI politics and the AI buildout

insights.claim: Democratic opposition to the AI buildout will likely run on two tracks: governors pausing local data center projects and Democrats in Congress working on AI legislation, probably not passed until a new president.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Data center suppliers face permitting and local-politics risk, with a 2028 timeline for federal rules.

insights.claim: A 30 percent hold-back in the data center buildout in 2028 is described as the base case, which would be bad for suppliers but far less severe than Thursday's selloff implied.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: The selloff priced a worse outcome than the speaker's own negative base case.

insights.claim: The speaker thinks AI regulation may not hurt hyperscalers, since limits on the frontier and on Chinese competition would let them shift compute from model development to selling inference.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Regulation can act as a moat for big incumbents, favoring them over data center suppliers.
insights.quote: Is that such a bad thing for the big AI? I'm not sure it is.

insights.claim: Thursday saw the largest one-day degrossing in the data (Morgan Stanley data back to 2016), with over 70 billion dollars wiped out in 90 minutes, as hedge funds unwound heavy AI exposure on the midterm-driven anti-AI sentiment.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: A forced washout of crowded AI positioning is a classic late-selloff signature.

insights.claim: The speaker is beginning to smell a bottom in the AI trade after the washout, comparing it to the spring software-space washout, while remaining worried about rates.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Entry opportunity in AI exposure if rates do not worsen.
insights.quote: I'm beginning to smell a bottom in here.

insights.claim: The firm's nowcast shows inflation rolling over sharply over two weeks, from about 50/50 odds of exceeding the latest print to near certainty it has rolled over, but nowcasts lead official data by about four to six weeks.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Soft inflation prints are likelier in coming months rather than in tomorrow's report.

insights.claim: Tomorrow's inflation report is expected to match consensus, but even a slight soft surprise could trigger an upward correction in the AI trade, and a soft trend could mean an abrupt end to the hiking season.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: The CPI print is the near-term catalyst for AI rebound.

insights.claim: The growth nowcast rose from about a 34 percent to a 45 percent chance, edging the US from the 'QE like' regime toward the 'gung-ho' regime.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: A regime shift toward gung-ho would favor risk assets and cyclical equity styles.

insights.claim: The nowcast should not steer oil forecasts now because of idiosyncratic factors (Iran war, diesel crisis), though it is useful for equity sectors, styles and FX pairs.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Use nowcast regimes for equities and FX but overlay judgment on oil.

themes.theme: Geopolitics: Ukraine peace talks and diesel

insights.claim: The speaker is skeptical that Russia truly wants to compromise in the Abu Dhabi talks, since its economy is doing okay and Putin sees no rush with two more years of a Trump presidency; Ukraine is willing to compromise.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Do not price a quick peace deal into markets.

insights.claim: The two key sticking points are where the border is drawn and security guarantees; a possible compromise is British, French and German troops west of the Dnieper with a demilitarized buffer on the east bank, though Russia is not ready.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Security guarantees, not reparations headlines, determine whether a deal is real.

insights.claim: Europe is not in the Abu Dhabi talks and is not at the Shenzhen meeting, so decisions on European security are being made above its head.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: European policy influence is limited, a risk for European assets tied to the security outcome.

insights.claim: Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries account for about one-third of the diesel crisis according to oil contacts, so peace could solve roughly a third of the diesel problem.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: A Ukraine deal would ease diesel supply, a disinflationary channel.

insights.claim: Peace progress in Ukraine and Iran would set up a Christmas rally and a rally into 2027; the speaker keeps a 'peace in Ukraine' basket ready.
insights.speaker: Host (Macro Mondays, solo)
insights.so_what: Peace is the upside scenario, with a prepared basket to deploy if talks advance.
insights.quote: boy would that be a setup for a uh a Christmas rally and a rally into 2027
